title: OpenColorful / Architecture Atlas
subtitle: A living map of the local-first assistant platform
sourceOfTruth: This manifest owns semantic module responsibilities, invariants, critical flows, and the files that anchor each boundary. Generated file inventory and import evidence are derived from the repository.

status.label: P1 Wave B in progress
status.summary: The repository is on the conversation workbench closeout lane. B0-B5b are implemented; B6 recorded bounded defects and deferred true-chain evidence.

layers.label: Product surfaces
layers.description: Where a person or operator enters the platform.

layers.label: Process and protocol boundary
layers.description: Stable cross-process vocabulary and transport adapters.

layers.label: Agent runtime
layers.description: Session execution, memory, skills, plugins, subagents, and observability.

layers.label: Persistence and host services
layers.description: Durable facts, credentials, process lifecycle, and local safety boundaries.

layers.label: Extension packages
layers.description: Public plugin protocol and runtime packages used by external integrations.

nodes.label: Desktop Electron shell
nodes.purpose: Owns the native window, preload capability boundary, supervisor proxy, SSE proxy, update flow, and packaged application lifecycle.
owns: Electron main process and window lifecycle
Local server proxy and restart-aware connection
invariants: Renderer never receives runtime credentials, arbitrary filesystem access, or direct Agent APIs.
The packaged server and plugin workspace dependencies must be verified before release.
Supervisor identity is checked before a proxy adopts a process.

nodes.label: Desktop React workbench
nodes.purpose: The product frontend: session-centric conversation, branch navigation, compaction and todo projections, memory, logs, usage, settings, and agent identity.
invariants: UI is read-only for session todo in Wave B; the first-party tool is the writer.
Renderer talks to the backend through the data source and preload bridge.
Live events and reload/restart state must converge to the same projection.

nodes.label: Web operator and test client
nodes.purpose: Browser-facing operational and protocol client. It is not the primary product frontend after G1.
owns: Web workspace, settings, plugin, skill, memory, logs, and subagent views
invariants: Web remains a client of the Server API; it does not import PI SDK internals.
New SSE event types must be admitted by the known-event registry.
User-facing changes need Web component coverage and browser evidence when in scope.

nodes.label: TUI protocol client
nodes.purpose: Terminal client that consumes Server protocols and remains independent from PI SDK imports.
invariants: TUI never bypasses Server to mutate Session state.
TUI does not import PI packages or src/pi-sdk.

nodes.label: Platform contracts
nodes.purpose: The cross-module and cross-process vocabulary: API inputs, events, session branches, memory, plugins, skills, subagents, observability, usage, and UI messages.
owns: Plugin protocol re-exports used by the host
invariants: Cross-process inputs are parsed, not trusted through type assertions.
Protocol version stays explicit and compatible.
Platform interfaces do not expose PI private types.

nodes.label: HTTP / SSE / WS server
nodes.purpose: Owns authentication boundary, input validation, route composition, event streams, WebSocket sessions, and transport projection.
owns: Session, message, branch, agent, memory, plugin, skill, subagent and usage routes
SSE replay subscription and WebSocket control
invariants: Routes parse and delegate; Agent business logic lives in Runtime and Services.
Events are written to Replay Store before broadcast.
Loopback binding and stable ApiError behavior remain the default boundary.

nodes.label: A2UI / TokUI projection
nodes.purpose: Projects structured platform events into bounded UI protocols. It is a one-way projection, never an alternate runtime.
invariants: Only the local fixed catalog and named handlers are accepted.
Raw HTML, scripts, javascript URLs, and arbitrary executable widgets are rejected.
Actions return to Server for validation.

nodes.label: Supervisor process host
nodes.purpose: Starts, monitors, health-checks, proxies, and stops the Agent Server while hosting the built client surface.
owns: Static Web asset hosting and transparent proxying
invariants: A health response must identify the expected child process before adoption.
Windows child process trees are cleaned up on stop.
Desktop and CLI both use the same local lifecycle concepts.

nodes.label: Session and execution runtime
nodes.purpose: The central orchestration layer: session lifecycle, prompt execution, model policy, tool policy, events, branches, usage, memory, plugins, skills, and subagent composition.
owns: Branch regenerate, fork, switch, and current-head recovery
Runtime composition for memory, skills, plugins, and subagents
invariants: Runtime owns Agent behavior; transport routes remain thin.
Session identity is a stable ID, never a file path.
The same runtime composition must be used after restart and branch actions.
Wave B branch and todo semantics remain append-only JSONL plus SQLite metadata/state.

nodes.label: PI SDK adapter boundary
nodes.purpose: The only direct import boundary to PI SDK. It turns PI sessions, models, tools, and events into OpenColorful platform interfaces.
invariants: Only src/pi-sdk may import @earendil-works/pi-*.
No PI private deep imports or duplicated Agent Loop implementation.
Platform interfaces do not leak PI private types.

nodes.label: Memory subsystem
nodes.purpose: Builds, injects, recalls, reviews, and applies memory with explicit policy and durable files/stores.
owns: Compile, summary, scheduler, and branch-aware reads
invariants: Memory is policy-governed and bounded; it is not an unconstrained self-modification loop.
Background review is advisory and must remain observable.
Memory content and operational logs have separate privacy boundaries.

nodes.label: Skills subsystem
nodes.purpose: Discovers, validates, trusts, installs, binds, snapshots, loads, and safely executes Skills from built-in, workspace, archive, Git, HTTP, plugin, OpenClaw, and Hermes sources.
owns: Manifest validation, readiness and risk assessment
Agent/session binding, snapshots and activation grants
Content loading, installation operations and script execution
invariants: A Skill is not executable merely because it was discovered; readiness, trust, risk and policy gates still apply.
Turn and Subagent Skill visibility is snapshot-based and bounded.
Plugin-provided Skills follow plugin lifecycle and fail closed when their source is disabled or removed.
Session files and external paths are validated against ownership and trusted roots.

nodes.label: Subagent runtime
nodes.purpose: Runs delegated work with parent-session control, mailbox delivery, artifact/transcript stores, policy leases, recovery, and observability.
owns: Workspace leases, recovery, and usage ingestion
invariants: Parent and child identities remain explicit.
Delivery and notification are separate concerns.
Capability and workspace policy are revalidated at execution boundaries.

nodes.label: SQLite metadata and state
nodes.purpose: Stores session metadata, branch heads, todo state, provider settings, plugin/skill registries, usage, observability, and platform state. It does not own message bodies.
owns: Session todos and durable event-related state
Provider, plugin, skill, usage, and observability stores
invariants: PI JSONL is the message and branch-history fact source.
SQLite never becomes a second message-body store.
Migrations are idempotent and recovery behavior is tested.

nodes.label: Config, sandbox and host safety
nodes.purpose: Defines local data paths, environment isolation, sandbox boundaries, directory selection, and host-level safety helpers.
owns: Native directory selection and path guards
invariants: Credentials stay in AuthStorage or dedicated secret stores.
Default network binding is loopback.
Paths are resolved through the central path contract.

nodes.label: Observability and usage
nodes.purpose: Captures activities, audits, diagnostics, traces, retention, safe values, support bundles, and usage evidence without leaking secrets.
owns: Activity, audit, diagnostic and emergency channels
Redaction, retention and support bundle policy
Runtime usage recording and query surfaces
invariants: Sensitive values are redacted before storage or projection.
Audit terminal state reflects the real domain outcome.
Operational evidence must be inspectable without becoming message content.

nodes.label: Plugin runtime and host
nodes.purpose: Loads, validates, grants, hosts, observes, and adapts plugin contributions from local, zip, Git, npm, OpenClaw, and Hermes sources.
owns: Capability grants, bindings, policy snapshots and host broker
Routes, tools, providers, surfaces, secrets, skills, and background contributions
invariants: Plugin execution is bounded by explicit capability policy.
Secret contribution uses dedicated stores and redaction.
Compatibility adapters normalize external ecosystems instead of leaking their formats inward.

nodes.label: @opencolorful/plugin-protocol
nodes.purpose: Public schemas and normalized vocabulary for manifests, permissions, contributions, IPC, compatibility, and snapshots.
invariants: Protocol package remains free of host implementation details.
Schema changes require compatibility tests and package build verification.

nodes.label: @opencolorful/plugin-sdk
nodes.purpose: Author-facing definitions, validation helpers, errors, and scaffolding for plugins.
invariants: SDK consumes the public protocol, not private host internals.
Generated scaffolds remain compatible with the runtime package.

nodes.label: @opencolorful/plugin-runtime + components
nodes.purpose: Runtime-side plugin server helpers and bounded UI/host contribution components.
invariants: Package APIs remain explicit and versionable.
Components do not take ownership of the host shell or permission lifecycle.

nodes.label: CLI and repository checks
nodes.purpose: Provides command-line lifecycle entry points plus the repository's import, package, document, smoke, and release checks.
invariants: Quality commands run separately and preserve exit codes.
Governance checks are part of the same quality story as product code.
Generated architecture data is stale when the manifest scan no longer matches it.

flows.label: Prompt → streamed answer
flows.summary: The normal conversation path: a client sends a command, the Server delegates to the Session Runtime, PI emits normalized events, Replay stores them, and the client projects the stream.

steps.label: Send
steps.detail: Composer sends through DesktopDataSource; Web and TUI are alternate clients.

steps.label: Validate and route
steps.detail: HTTP route parses the prompt and selects the existing runtime composition.

steps.label: Execute
steps.detail: SessionRuntime runs the turn, maps events, applies policy, and records usage.

steps.label: Delegate to PI
steps.detail: Only this boundary imports the PI SDK and exposes stable platform types.

steps.label: Persist and replay
steps.detail: Message and branch history remain in PI JSONL; metadata and replay state use SQLite-backed stores.

steps.label: Project
steps.detail: The client adopts the stream and projects events into conversation, tools, memory, and workbench surfaces.

flows.label: Wave B: regenerate / branch / fork
flows.summary: Wave B uses PI tree primitives behind a stable API. Old branches remain in JSONL; the selected branch head and todo state are durable SQLite metadata.

steps.label: Choose a turn
steps.detail: Timeline and branch switcher use stable entryId, branchId, and turnId anchors.

steps.label: Apply semantics
steps.detail: Server returns stable 400/404/409 errors and never silently aborts a running turn.

steps.label: Create or switch
steps.detail: Regenerate shares the normal prompt path; fork uses a detached manager; branch switch persists the selected head.

steps.label: Use PI tree
steps.detail: The adapter hides PI SessionManager and AgentSession tree primitives.

steps.label: Recover
steps.detail: JSONL remains append-only; SQLite stores branch head and session-owned todo state.

steps.label: Re-project
steps.detail: Live events and restart/replay state must converge to the same desktop view.

flows.label: Memory activation cycle
flows.summary: Memory remains a bounded subsystem around the conversation loop: policy decides what is injected, tools and recall expose controlled access, and background review produces advisory intent.

steps.label: Resolve policy
steps.detail: The runtime decides when memory context and tools are available.

steps.label: Recall and write intent
steps.detail: Memory tools, injection, recall, and background review operate through explicit contracts.

steps.label: Persist facts
steps.detail: Memory stores and files retain durable state while session messages remain PI JSONL-owned.

steps.label: Record evidence
steps.detail: Memory activity and audit outcomes remain inspectable without leaking sensitive content.

steps.label: Feed the next turn
steps.detail: The next prompt receives only the policy-approved, bounded memory projection.

flows.label: Plugin lifecycle
flows.summary: External plugin formats are normalized into a host-owned capability system, then executed through bounded carriers and observed through the same platform services.

steps.label: Author
steps.detail: A plugin author uses definePlugin and the public protocol types.

steps.label: Validate
steps.detail: Manifest, permissions, contributions, compatibility, and IPC schemas are checked.

steps.label: Host
steps.detail: The host installs sources, resolves grants, loads runtimes, and exposes bounded contributions.

steps.label: Enforce
steps.detail: Capability snapshots, sandbox bridges, path guards, and secret stores constrain execution.

steps.label: Observe
steps.detail: Plugin activity, audit and diagnostics use the shared safe-value and trace model.

flows.label: Skill lifecycle
flows.summary: A Skill moves from source discovery through validation and readiness gates to a bounded per-turn snapshot. Installation, binding and script execution remain policy-controlled.

steps.label: Discover sources
steps.detail: The composition root scans built-in, workspace, managed, ecosystem and plugin sources into one catalog.

steps.label: Validate and assess
steps.detail: Manifest, compatibility, readiness, risk and trust determine whether a candidate can be used.

steps.label: Persist bindings
steps.detail: Bundles, agent bindings, session bindings, activation grants and operations are stored durably.

steps.label: Enforce trust and execution
steps.detail: Trusted roots, path safety, sandbox ports and confirmation tokens gate content and scripts.

steps.label: Freeze per turn
steps.detail: The prompt path receives a bounded Skill snapshot; a later catalog mutation cannot silently expand the active turn.

steps.label: Load on demand
steps.detail: Content reads consume the frozen snapshot and activation overlay instead of arbitrary filesystem paths.

flows.label: Desktop startup and release
flows.summary: Electron launches the local Supervisor, which hosts the Server and client assets. The preload and proxy keep the renderer behind an explicit capability boundary.

steps.label: Launch
steps.detail: Electron creates the window and starts the local connection strategy.

steps.label: Host
steps.detail: Supervisor starts or adopts the expected Agent Server and serves the built client.

steps.label: Serve
steps.detail: The Hono server owns runtime state and protocol endpoints.

steps.label: Render
steps.detail: The renderer receives only shell operations and backend data through the approved data source.

knownGaps.title: Wave B true-chain evidence is not complete
knownGaps.detail: Compact live/replay identity and durable todo true-chain coverage are still deferred to the closeout evidence; the architecture map records them as implemented code plus incomplete verification.

knownGaps.title: BRANCH-03/04 send-disabled defect remains bounded
knownGaps.detail: The post-branch-switch send path remains a known defect from B3/B6 and must not be silently represented as complete.

knownGaps.title: Web event allowlist follow-up
knownGaps.detail: The Web protocol client still needs the additive todo.updated event declaration tracked in the Wave B closeout.

rules.label: Server-first
rules.detail: Desktop, Web, and TUI consume HTTP/SSE/WS or the explicit Electron bridge; they do not mutate Runtime state directly.

rules.label: Data ownership
rules.detail: PI JSONL owns message bodies and branch history. SQLite owns metadata, indexes, platform state, branch heads, todos, usage, and registries.

rules.label: Replay before broadcast
rules.detail: An event is durable in the Replay Store before it is sent to SSE or WebSocket subscribers.

rules.label: Host-owned extension points
rules.detail: Plugins contribute through bounded contracts; the host retains layout, permissions, lifecycle, and security policy.
